Names of the numeric channels of one controller

Source: R/channel_layout.R
channel_layout.Rd

analog_channels() names its columns by key, as player() does for buttons. A measurement that several formats record has one key in all of them, whatever the format calls it:

Usage

channel_layout(movie, idx = 1L)

Arguments

movie

A replayr_movie or replayr_poll_stream returned by read_movie() or a format-specific reader.

idx

Player index, 1-based. Defaults to 1 (player 1).

Value

Data frame with one row per channel: column, key, and name, the label of the field in the recording or, for formats without labels, a description of the field.

Details

  • left_x, left_y, right_x, right_y: the axes of the analogue sticks. The N64 stick, the 3DS Circle Pad and the Nunchuk stick are the left stick; the 3DS C-stick is the right one.

  • left_trigger, right_trigger: analogue triggers.

  • mouse_dx, mouse_dy: movement of a mouse since the previous observation. mouse_x and mouse_y are positions.

  • touch_x, touch_y: position on a touch surface.

  • aim_x, aim_y: where a light gun points.

  • accel_x, accel_y, accel_z and gyro_x, gyro_y, gyro_z: motion sensors.

Every other channel has the key formed from its own name in lower case, such as tilt_x for the BizHawk field Tilt X. Where two channels of a controller would take one shared key, each keeps the key of its own name. Only the names are shared: values keep the range and unit of their source (see analog_channels()).

See also

button_layout() for the digital controls.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "paper", "mouse-drag.bk2", package = "replayr")
channel_layout(read_movie(path))
#>   column      key                   name
#> 1      1 mouse_dx P1 Motion Left / Right
#> 2      2 mouse_dy    P1 Motion Up / Down
